Job Description
Job Description About the Business Telus Digital AI Data Solutions (TI AI) has been a trailblazer in data services since 2005, recently debuting on the NYSE on February 21 . TI AI is known for delivering high-quality datasets critical for training and validating machine learning models—especially in the field of computer vision. Our in-house labeling platform, GT Studio, powers a wide array of data solutions across industries, with a special focus on autonomous vehicles and emerging computer vision use cases. As we continue to grow, our mission remains the same: to provide cutting-edge, reliable datasets that help AI teams around the world build better, safer, and more effective models. About the Team The Telus Digital AI team partners closely with clients to define data annotation and collection strategies, ensuring successful delivery through expert consulting and execution. Our Technical Project Management team sits at the center of this process, supporting post-sales execution and serving as the bridge between client needs and technical delivery. Overview We are seeking an experienced Associate Project Manager with a strong interest in AI and computer vision to lead data annotation and labeling projects for enterprise clients. This role involves managing multiple initiatives, coordinating cross-functional teams, and ensuring timely, high-quality delivery across AI/ML programs. The ideal candidate brings solid project management skills, an understanding of technical workflows, and a passion for delivering impactful results in a fast-moving tech environment. Key Responsibilities Serve as the main point of contact for clients post-sale, translating project goals into clear action plans. Lead the planning and delivery of AI/ML projects—especially those focused on computer vision and data annotation. Collaborate with solution engineers, data specialists, and QA teams to manage both automated and manual labeling workflows. Monitor project performance, identify risks, and drive resolution of issues to keep initiatives on track. Coordinate resource planning, reporting, and timeline tracking using industry-standard tools and practices. Partner with internal teams (engineering, R&D, and product) to communicate client feedback and align on project goals. Contribute to process improvements and best practice documentation to enhance delivery efficiency and consistency. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in a technical or related field (STEM preferred) project management experience, ideally in AI /ML, software engineering, or data-driven environment. Strong organizational and communication skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities. Familiarity with AI/ML concepts, computer vision, or data annotation workflows is a plus. Experience working with cross-functional teams in dynamic, client-facing roles. Comfort with tools such as Monday.com, Clickup, JIRA, Trello, Asana, or similar project management platforms. A proactive mindset, collaborative spirit, and desire to grow within a high-tech, fast-evolving space. Willingness to travel occasionally, if required. Why Join Us? At TI AI, you’ll work with industry leaders shaping the future of AI-powered solutions. You’ll gain exposure to cutting-edge projects, play a key role in delivering high-impact work, and grow your career in one of the most exciting fields in tech.

companies.description:
Trexquant is a systematic hedge fund where we use thousands of statistical algorithms to trade equity, futures and other markets globally. Starting with many data sets, we develop large sets of features and use various machine learning methods to discover trading signals and effectively combine them into market-neutral portfolios. We are looking for data scientists, physicists, engineers, economists and programmers to develop the next generation of machine learning strategies that can accurately predict the future movements of liquid financial assets. Our Quantitative Researchers are embedded within the following teams: Alpha Researcher: As a member of the Alpha Researcher team, you will be involved in developing market-neutral signals, parsing and analyzing large data sets and collaborating with the Data and Strategy Research team to build a diverse set of predictive models. Data Scientist: As a member of the Data Science team, you will be involved in parsing and analyzing large data sets, working on discovering and obtaining new sources of data and collaborating with the Alpha and Strategy team to build predictive machine learning models. Strategy Researcher: As a member of the Strategy team, you will be developing systematic strategies based on a variety of machine learning and statistical methods. The data you train and validate comes from actual market trading When you apply for a Quantitative Researcher role at Trexquant, we will first assess you on the core skills required for the Quantitative Researcher. During the interview process, we will be able to get to know you better, learn about your strengths and match you to the best research team that closely aligns with your skills and preference. Your Responsibilities: Design, implement, and optimize various machine learning models aimed at predicting liquid assets using a wide set of financial data and a vast library of trading signals Parse data sets to be used for future alpha(strategy) development Investigate and implement state-of-the-art academic research in the field of quantitative finance Collaborate with experienced and resourceful quantitative researchers to carry out experiments and test hypothesis using simulations Requirements Graduate degree (Bachelors, Masters, or PhD) in any STEM discipline from a prestigious institution Passion for machine learning and quantitative finance Strong problem-solving skills Ability to work effectively both as an individual and a team player Proficient in programming languages such as Python Previous experience in alpha research and the development of trading signals and strategies The role is also open for candidates graduating from Tier 1 campuses in 2027 Benefits Competitive compensation with bonus tied to the performance of algorithms you develop Work in a collaborative and friendly environment, participate in decision-making process for research direction, and have opportunity to lead on new ideas Pre-tax commuter benefits Weekly company meals

PLACEMENT	Quantitative Researcher	9160000 INR			8.0

Job Description
Description Trexquant is a systematic hedge fund where we use thousands of statistical algorithms to trade equity, futures and other markets globally. Starting with many data sets, we develop large sets of features and use various machine learning methods to discover trading signals and effectively combine them into market-neutral portfolios. We are looking for data scientists, physicists, engineers, economists and programmers to develop the next generation of machine learning strategies that can accurately predict the future movements of liquid financial assets. Our Quantitative Researchers are embedded within the following teams: Alpha Researcher: As a member of the Alpha Researcher team, you will be involved in developing market-neutral signals, parsing and analyzing large data sets and collaborating with the Data and Strategy Research team to build a diverse set of predictive models. Data Scientist: As a member of the Data Science team, you will be involved in parsing and analyzing large data sets, working on discovering and obtaining new sources of data and collaborating with the Alpha and Strategy team to build predictive machine learning models. Strategy Researcher: As a member of the Strategy team, you will be developing systematic strategies based on a variety of machine learning and statistical methods. The data you train and validate comes from actual market trading When you apply for a Quantitative Researcher role at Trexquant, we will first assess you on the core skills required for the Quantitative Researcher. During the interview process, we will be able to get to know you better, learn about your strengths and match you to the best research team that closely aligns with your skills and preference. Your Responsibilities: Design, implement, and optimize various machine learning models aimed at predicting liquid assets using a wide set of financial data and a vast library of trading signals Parse data sets to be used for future alpha(strategy) development Investigate and implement state-of-the-art academic research in the field of quantitative finance Collaborate with experienced and resourceful quantitative researchers to carry out experiments and test hypothesis using simulations Requirements Graduate degree (Bachelors, Masters, or PhD) in any STEM discipline from a prestigious institution Passion for machine learning and quantitative finance Strong problem-solving skills Ability to work effectively both as an individual and a team player Proficient in programming languages such as Python Previous experience in alpha research and the development of trading signals and strategies The role is also open for candidates graduating from Tier 1 campuses in 2027 Benefits Competitive compensation with bonus tied to the performance of algorithms you develop Work in a collaborative and friendly environment, participate in decision-making process for research direction, and have opportunity to lead on new ideas Pre-tax commuter benefits Weekly company meals

About the company	Trexquant has continuously improved its investment and research platform since starting operations in April 2014. Our firm was founded on the principles of traditional quantitative finance. However, our commitment to leveraging new and emerging technologies, particularly machine learning and data science, has enabled us to stand out in the industry today. We use rigorous quantitative methods with the objective of creating market-neutral equity portfolios in global equity markets. To do this, we develop trading signals (or Alphas) using our vast and continuously growing collection of data variables. Our proprietary backtesting platform helps us refine these signals until we’re confident they’re ready for production. The strategy team then uses the Alphas as inputs for more complex trading models called Strategies. The result is an ever-growing and adapting engine built from thousands of intricate models and tens of thousands of signals, tailor-made and continuously engineered to outperform and seek profit from the market in all market conditions.

Job Description
Description Trexquant is a systematic hedge fund where we use thousands of statistical algorithms to trade equity, futures and other markets globally. Starting with many data sets, we develop large sets of features and use various machine learning methods to discover trading signals and effectively combine them into market-neutral portfolios. We are looking for data scientists, physicists, engineers, economists and programmers to develop the next generation of machine learning strategies that can accurately predict the future movements of liquid financial assets. Our Quantitative Researchers are embedded within the following teams: Alpha Researcher: As a member of the Alpha Researcher team, you will be involved in developing market-neutral signals, parsing and analyzing large data sets and collaborating with the Data and Strategy Research team to build a diverse set of predictive models. Data Scientist: As a member of the Data Science team, you will be involved in parsing and analyzing large data sets, working on discovering and obtaining new sources of data and collaborating with the Alpha and Strategy team to build predictive machine learning models. Strategy Researcher: As a member of the Strategy team, you will be developing systematic strategies based on a variety of machine learning and statistical methods. The data you train and validate comes from actual market trading When you apply for a Quantitative Researcher role at Trexquant, we will first assess you on the core skills required for the Quantitative Researcher. During the interview process, we will be able to get to know you better, learn about your strengths and match you to the best research team that closely aligns with your skills and preference. Your Responsibilities: Design, implement, and optimize various machine learning models aimed at predicting liquid assets using a wide set of financial data and a vast library of trading signals Parse data sets to be used for future alpha(strategy) development Investigate and implement state-of-the-art academic research in the field of quantitative finance Collaborate with experienced and resourceful quantitative researchers to carry out experiments and test hypothesis using simulations Requirements Graduate degree (Bachelors, Masters, or PhD) in any STEM discipline from a prestigious institution Passion for machine learning and quantitative finance Strong problem-solving skills Ability to work effectively both as an individual and a team player Proficient in programming languages such as Python Previous experience in alpha research and the development of trading signals and strategies The role is also open for candidates graduating from Tier 1 campuses in 2027 Benefits Competitive compensation with bonus tied to the performance of algorithms you develop Work in a collaborative and friendly environment, participate in decision-making process for research direction, and have opportunity to lead on new ideas Pre-tax commuter benefits Weekly company meals

That is why we are committed to creating a work environment that actively values, appreciates, and respects everyone. We encourage applications from people with a wide variety of backgrounds and experiences. Consider a career at WMG and get the best of both worlds – an innovative global music company that retains the creative spirit of a nimble independent.

companies.description:
About Waterfly Over water, shippers choose between ships that take days and aircraft that cost about 20 times more. Waterfly, incubated at IIT Madras, is building the mode in between: electric, autonomous craft that fly just above the sea at near-aircraft speed for a tenth of the cost of air freight. What to Expect We are hiring Management Consultants from the 2027 batch to work with our clients and turn them into long-term partners. You will work directly with the CEO and CBO, own a set of client accounts within your first few months, and take each one from first meeting to a signed pilot or partnership. The role is full-time and based in Chennai, with travel to ports, client sites and partners in India and abroad. You will join in summer 2027 and report to the CBO. Our 300 kg craft has flown autonomously since August 2026, and port pilots are planned from December 2026. Our first clients are ports, ship managers, offshore operators and island administrations that need cargo moved over water in hours, not days. Each has a different problem, and our next craft is still being shaped, so the case you build for a client also shapes what we build. Expect direct mentorship from the founders, real ownership of client relationships early on, and the pace of a company bringing a new kind of vehicle to its first customers. What You’ll Do • Client case studies. Study each client’s cargo, routes, volumes and current costs, and build the case for how our craft cuts their delivery time and cost. • Proposals and pilots. Turn each case into a proposal with pricing, a pilot plan and success measures, and help run the pilot once it starts. • Partnerships. Convert successful pilots into long-term partnerships and orders, and write up the results as case studies that win the next client. • Client relationships. Own your accounts from first meeting to signed agreement: regular updates, site visits, and the follow-through that keeps every commitment on track. • New clients. Find and qualify new clients across shipping, ports, offshore energy and island logistics, open the first conversations, and bring what you learn back to the team. What You’ll Bring • Structured problem-solving. You can turn an ambiguous client problem into a model, find the data and reach an answer you can defend. • Strong spreadsheet and financial modelling skills: unit economics, pricing, cost comparisons and scenarios. • Clear writing and storytelling. You can produce a proposal or deck that a port authority or logistics head can act on.• Confidence with clients. You can run a meeting with a senior client, listen well, and follow it through to a decision. • Comfort with technical depth. You will learn how the craft works well enough to discuss payload, range and charging with engineers and clients. • High ownership and speed. You care about getting the first cargo flying, not about whose job something is. • Good to have: consulting, business development or startup internships; case competitions; knowledge of shipping, ports, logistics or aviation; experience with CRM tools.

Job Description
About Waterfly Over water, shippers choose between ships that take days and aircraft that cost about 20 times more. Waterfly, incubated at IIT Madras, is building the mode in between: electric, autonomous craft that fly just above the sea at near-aircraft speed for a tenth of the cost of air freight. What to Expect We are hiring Management Consultants from the 2027 batch to work with our clients and turn them into long-term partners. You will work directly with the CEO and CBO, own a set of client accounts within your first few months, and take each one from first meeting to a signed pilot or partnership. The role is full-time and based in Chennai, with travel to ports, client sites and partners in India and abroad. You will join in summer 2027 and report to the CBO. Our 300 kg craft has flown autonomously since August 2026, and port pilots are planned from December 2026. Our first clients are ports, ship managers, offshore operators and island administrations that need cargo moved over water in hours, not days. Each has a different problem, and our next craft is still being shaped, so the case you build for a client also shapes what we build. Expect direct mentorship from the founders, real ownership of client relationships early on, and the pace of a company bringing a new kind of vehicle to its first customers. What You’ll Do • Client case studies. Study each client’s cargo, routes, volumes and current costs, and build the case for how our craft cuts their delivery time and cost. • Proposals and pilots. Turn each case into a proposal with pricing, a pilot plan and success measures, and help run the pilot once it starts. • Partnerships. Convert successful pilots into long-term partnerships and orders, and write up the results as case studies that win the next client. • Client relationships. Own your accounts from first meeting to signed agreement: regular updates, site visits, and the follow-through that keeps every commitment on track. • New clients. Find and qualify new clients across shipping, ports, offshore energy and island logistics, open the first conversations, and bring what you learn back to the team. What You’ll Bring • Structured problem-solving. You can turn an ambiguous client problem into a model, find the data and reach an answer you can defend. • Strong spreadsheet and financial modelling skills: unit economics, pricing, cost comparisons and scenarios. • Clear writing and storytelling. You can produce a proposal or deck that a port authority or logistics head can act on.• Confidence with clients. You can run a meeting with a senior client, listen well, and follow it through to a decision. • Comfort with technical depth. You will learn how the craft works well enough to discuss payload, range and charging with engineers and clients. • High ownership and speed. You care about getting the first cargo flying, not about whose job something is. • Good to have: consulting, business development or startup internships; case competitions; knowledge of shipping, ports, logistics or aviation; experience with CRM tools.

companies.description:
About Waterfly Waterfly builds electric, autonomous craft that fly a few metres above the sea, moving cargo at nearaircraft speed for a tenth of the cost of air freight. We started at IIT Madras, build every craft in-house in Chennai, and aim to be the cheapest and fastest way to move goods across the world. What to Expect We are hiring Graduate Engineers from the 2027 batch to design and analyse Pelican, our 10-tonne electric sea-skimming cargo craft. You will join a small team of engineers who take the craft from a blank page to a flight test, with your focus on CAD, CFD and FEA, and you will own the analysis of a subsystem within your first few months. The role is full-time and based in Chennai, with travel to test sites. You will join in summer 2027 and report to the CTO. The engineering has no textbook answer yet. Flying in ground effect cuts drag and adds lift, giving better lift-to-drag in our tests, and that is what lets a battery-powered craft cover real distances. Our patent pending blended wing-hull-body has scaled from a 3 kg model in 2025 to the 300 kg Hummingbird, which has flown autonomously since August 2026. Aerodynamics, hydrodynamics, structures, batteries, avionics and autonomy sit in one team, so your models become carbon-fibre parts within weeks, and flight data tells you how good they were. Expect direct mentorship from the founders, fast and honest feedback, and a pace that picks up around test campaigns. What You’ll Do Design. Build and own CAD models of the craft and its subsystems: wings and hull, hydrofoils, composite structure, battery and motor installations. Start with hand calculations, then turn them into geometry our workshop can build. • Simulate. Run CFD on aerodynamics in ground effect and on planing and take-off hydrodynamics, and FEA on composite structures under flight, landing and wave loads. Set up meshes, boundary conditions and convergence checks you can defend. • Validate. Compare your models with hand calculations, coupon tests and data from lake and sea trials, and fix the model or the design when they disagree. • Document for certification. Produce the design, analysis and safety evidence that class societies such as Bureau Veritas and the Indian Register of Shipping need to approve a new type of vessel. • Work across the stack. Help build what you design in our workshop, support teammates on other subsystems, take part in design reviews, and pick up whatever the craft needs that week. What You’ll Bring • A strong grasp of physics and maths. You reach for a first-principles estimate before a simulation.• Hands-on experience with CAD and at least one of CFD or FEA, from coursework, research or a project, and the judgement to spot a result that cannot be right. • Depth in aerodynamics, hydrodynamics, or structures and composites, and real curiosity about the rest. • Python or MATLAB to automate analysis, run parameter sweeps and post-process results. • You have designed or built real hardware, such as a competition vehicle, drone, rocket, robot, boat or your own project, and can explain what broke and why. • High ownership and speed. You care about getting the craft flying, not about whose job something is. • Clear writing. You can produce an analysis report that someone else can act on. • Good to have: composite laminate or buckling analysis; free-surface or ground-effect CFD; planing hulls or hydrofoils; tools such as SolidWorks, CATIA, ANSYS, Abaqus, STAR-CCM+ or OpenFOAM; or a student team such as Formula Student, solar car, aero-design, AUV or rocketry.

Job Description
About Waterfly Waterfly builds electric, autonomous craft that fly a few metres above the sea, moving cargo at nearaircraft speed for a tenth of the cost of air freight. We started at IIT Madras, build every craft in-house in Chennai, and aim to be the cheapest and fastest way to move goods across the world. What to Expect We are hiring Graduate Engineers from the 2027 batch to design and analyse Pelican, our 10-tonne electric sea-skimming cargo craft. You will join a small team of engineers who take the craft from a blank page to a flight test, with your focus on CAD, CFD and FEA, and you will own the analysis of a subsystem within your first few months. The role is full-time and based in Chennai, with travel to test sites. You will join in summer 2027 and report to the CTO. The engineering has no textbook answer yet. Flying in ground effect cuts drag and adds lift, giving better lift-to-drag in our tests, and that is what lets a battery-powered craft cover real distances. Our patent pending blended wing-hull-body has scaled from a 3 kg model in 2025 to the 300 kg Hummingbird, which has flown autonomously since August 2026. Aerodynamics, hydrodynamics, structures, batteries, avionics and autonomy sit in one team, so your models become carbon-fibre parts within weeks, and flight data tells you how good they were. Expect direct mentorship from the founders, fast and honest feedback, and a pace that picks up around test campaigns. What You’ll Do Design. Build and own CAD models of the craft and its subsystems: wings and hull, hydrofoils, composite structure, battery and motor installations. Start with hand calculations, then turn them into geometry our workshop can build. • Simulate. Run CFD on aerodynamics in ground effect and on planing and take-off hydrodynamics, and FEA on composite structures under flight, landing and wave loads. Set up meshes, boundary conditions and convergence checks you can defend. • Validate. Compare your models with hand calculations, coupon tests and data from lake and sea trials, and fix the model or the design when they disagree. • Document for certification. Produce the design, analysis and safety evidence that class societies such as Bureau Veritas and the Indian Register of Shipping need to approve a new type of vessel. • Work across the stack. Help build what you design in our workshop, support teammates on other subsystems, take part in design reviews, and pick up whatever the craft needs that week. What You’ll Bring • A strong grasp of physics and maths. You reach for a first-principles estimate before a simulation.• Hands-on experience with CAD and at least one of CFD or FEA, from coursework, research or a project, and the judgement to spot a result that cannot be right. • Depth in aerodynamics, hydrodynamics, or structures and composites, and real curiosity about the rest. • Python or MATLAB to automate analysis, run parameter sweeps and post-process results. • You have designed or built real hardware, such as a competition vehicle, drone, rocket, robot, boat or your own project, and can explain what broke and why. • High ownership and speed. You care about getting the craft flying, not about whose job something is. • Clear writing. You can produce an analysis report that someone else can act on. • Good to have: composite laminate or buckling analysis; free-surface or ground-effect CFD; planing hulls or hydrofoils; tools such as SolidWorks, CATIA, ANSYS, Abaqus, STAR-CCM+ or OpenFOAM; or a student team such as Formula Student, solar car, aero-design, AUV or rocketry.

Job Description
About Waterfly Waterfly builds electric, autonomous craft that fly a few metres above the sea, moving cargo at nearaircraft speed for a tenth of the cost of air freight. We started at IIT Madras, build every craft in-house in Chennai, and aim to be the cheapest and fastest way to move goods across the world. What to Expect We are hiring Graduate Engineers from the 2027 batch to design and analyse Pelican, our 10-tonne electric sea-skimming cargo craft. You will join a small team of engineers who take the craft from a blank page to a flight test, with your focus on CAD, CFD and FEA, and you will own the analysis of a subsystem within your first few months. The role is full-time and based in Chennai, with travel to test sites. You will join in summer 2027 and report to the CTO. The engineering has no textbook answer yet. Flying in ground effect cuts drag and adds lift, giving better lift-to-drag in our tests, and that is what lets a battery-powered craft cover real distances. Our patent pending blended wing-hull-body has scaled from a 3 kg model in 2025 to the 300 kg Hummingbird, which has flown autonomously since August 2026. Aerodynamics, hydrodynamics, structures, batteries, avionics and autonomy sit in one team, so your models become carbon-fibre parts within weeks, and flight data tells you how good they were. Expect direct mentorship from the founders, fast and honest feedback, and a pace that picks up around test campaigns. What You’ll Do Design. Build and own CAD models of the craft and its subsystems: wings and hull, hydrofoils, composite structure, battery and motor installations. Start with hand calculations, then turn them into geometry our workshop can build. • Simulate. Run CFD on aerodynamics in ground effect and on planing and take-off hydrodynamics, and FEA on composite structures under flight, landing and wave loads. Set up meshes, boundary conditions and convergence checks you can defend. • Validate. Compare your models with hand calculations, coupon tests and data from lake and sea trials, and fix the model or the design when they disagree. • Document for certification. Produce the design, analysis and safety evidence that class societies such as Bureau Veritas and the Indian Register of Shipping need to approve a new type of vessel. • Work across the stack. Help build what you design in our workshop, support teammates on other subsystems, take part in design reviews, and pick up whatever the craft needs that week. What You’ll Bring • A strong grasp of physics and maths. You reach for a first-principles estimate before a simulation.• Hands-on experience with CAD and at least one of CFD or FEA, from coursework, research or a project, and the judgement to spot a result that cannot be right. • Depth in aerodynamics, hydrodynamics, or structures and composites, and real curiosity about the rest. • Python or MATLAB to automate analysis, run parameter sweeps and post-process results. • You have designed or built real hardware, such as a competition vehicle, drone, rocket, robot, boat or your own project, and can explain what broke and why. • High ownership and speed. You care about getting the craft flying, not about whose job something is. • Clear writing. You can produce an analysis report that someone else can act on. • Good to have: composite laminate or buckling analysis; free-surface or ground-effect CFD; planing hulls or hydrofoils; tools such as SolidWorks, CATIA, ANSYS, Abaqus, STAR-CCM+ or OpenFOAM; or a student team such as Formula Student, solar car, aero-design, AUV or rocketry.

companies.description:
About Waterfly Over water, shippers choose between ships that take days and aircraft that cost about 20 times more. Waterfly, incubated at IIT Madras, is building the mode in between: electric, autonomous craft that fly just above the sea at near-aircraft speed for a tenth of the cost of air freight. What to Expect We are hiring a Growth Strategist from the 2027 batch to grow Waterfly’s reach: new client leads, a presence at the right events, and the people and institutions that help us scale. You will work directly with the CEO and CBO, own our outreach pipeline within your first few months, and hand qualified leads to the team that turns them into pilots. The role is full-time and based in Chennai, with travel to events, campuses and partners in India and abroad. You will join in summer 2027 and report to the CBO. Our 300 kg craft has flown autonomously since August 2026, and port pilots are planned from December 2026. A new kind of vehicle has to be seen and understood before anyone buys it: by ports, ship managers, offshore operators and island administrations, and by the engineers and institutions who will build it with us. Every lead, event and partnership you open moves us closer to paying cargo. Expect direct mentorship from the founders, the freedom to try new channels and keep what works, and the pace of a company bringing a new kind of vehicle to its first customers. What You’ll Do • Lead generation. Find potential clients across shipping, ports, offshore energy, logistics and island supply through research, industry directories, LinkedIn, referrals and cold outreach, and qualify them before handing them to the team. • Outreach campaigns. Run targeted outreach by email, phone and social media, track every lead in a CRM, and test which channels start the best conversations. • Events and exhibitions. Find the maritime, logistics, aerospace and deep-tech events worth attending, secure stands, talks and demos, and turn each event into meetings and leads. • Recruitment. Run hiring with the founders: campus placements and pre-placement talks, sourcing and screening candidates, and organising interviews and work trials. • Institutional partnerships. Build partnerships with universities, research labs, industry bodies and government institutions for research, testing, talent and visibility. What You’ll Bring • A structured, data-driven approach. You set targets, track a funnel and change course when the numbers say so. • Strong research skills. You can find the right company, and the right person in it, from scattered sources. • Clear writing and storytelling. You can write an email, post or pitch that gets a busy person to reply.• Confidence with people. You can open a conversation with a port official, an event organiser, a professor or a candidate, and follow it through. • Comfort with technical depth. You will learn how the craft works well enough to explain it to clients, partners and engineers. • High ownership and speed. You care about getting the first cargo flying, not about whose job something is. • Good to have: sales, business development, marketing or recruiting internships; organising a fest, conference or club event; experience with CRM or outreach tools; content, video or design skills.

Job Description
About Waterfly Over water, shippers choose between ships that take days and aircraft that cost about 20 times more. Waterfly, incubated at IIT Madras, is building the mode in between: electric, autonomous craft that fly just above the sea at near-aircraft speed for a tenth of the cost of air freight. What to Expect We are hiring a Growth Strategist from the 2027 batch to grow Waterfly’s reach: new client leads, a presence at the right events, and the people and institutions that help us scale. You will work directly with the CEO and CBO, own our outreach pipeline within your first few months, and hand qualified leads to the team that turns them into pilots. The role is full-time and based in Chennai, with travel to events, campuses and partners in India and abroad. You will join in summer 2027 and report to the CBO. Our 300 kg craft has flown autonomously since August 2026, and port pilots are planned from December 2026. A new kind of vehicle has to be seen and understood before anyone buys it: by ports, ship managers, offshore operators and island administrations, and by the engineers and institutions who will build it with us. Every lead, event and partnership you open moves us closer to paying cargo. Expect direct mentorship from the founders, the freedom to try new channels and keep what works, and the pace of a company bringing a new kind of vehicle to its first customers. What You’ll Do • Lead generation. Find potential clients across shipping, ports, offshore energy, logistics and island supply through research, industry directories, LinkedIn, referrals and cold outreach, and qualify them before handing them to the team. • Outreach campaigns. Run targeted outreach by email, phone and social media, track every lead in a CRM, and test which channels start the best conversations. • Events and exhibitions. Find the maritime, logistics, aerospace and deep-tech events worth attending, secure stands, talks and demos, and turn each event into meetings and leads. • Recruitment. Run hiring with the founders: campus placements and pre-placement talks, sourcing and screening candidates, and organising interviews and work trials. • Institutional partnerships. Build partnerships with universities, research labs, industry bodies and government institutions for research, testing, talent and visibility. What You’ll Bring • A structured, data-driven approach. You set targets, track a funnel and change course when the numbers say so. • Strong research skills. You can find the right company, and the right person in it, from scattered sources. • Clear writing and storytelling. You can write an email, post or pitch that gets a busy person to reply.• Confidence with people. You can open a conversation with a port official, an event organiser, a professor or a candidate, and follow it through. • Comfort with technical depth. You will learn how the craft works well enough to explain it to clients, partners and engineers. • High ownership and speed. You care about getting the first cargo flying, not about whose job something is. • Good to have: sales, business development, marketing or recruiting internships; organising a fest, conference or club event; experience with CRM or outreach tools; content, video or design skills.

companies.description:
About Waterfly Over water, shippers choose between ships that take days and aircraft that cost about 20 times more. Waterfly, incubated at IIT Madras, is building the mode in between: electric, autonomous craft that fly just above the sea at near-aircraft speed for a tenth of the cost of air freight. What to Expect We are hiring Management Consultants from the 2027 batch to map, and help shape, the rules that let a new kind of vehicle operate. You will work directly with the CEO and CBO, own a regulatory area within your first few months, and turn what you find into plans the company can act on. The role is full-time and based in Chennai, with travel to regulators, class societies and partners. You will join in summer 2027 and report to the CBO. Our craft fly a few metres above the water, so they are regulated as vessels, not aircraft: Type B wing-inground craft under IMO guidelines, and vessels under India’s Merchant Shipping Act, 2025. That is a faster path, but much of it has never been applied to an uncrewed, battery-electric craft with a blended wing-hull-body, or to the charging stations, offshore data centres, and defence and government uses around it. Your work decides how fast our 300 kg craft, flying autonomously since August 2026, and its successors reach paying customers. Expect direct mentorship from the founders, a seat in conversations with regulators and class societies early on, and enough engineering exposure to understand exactly what you are getting approved. What You’ll Do • Craft regulation. Study the rules for blended wing-hull-body craft and other new designs, including IMO wing-in-ground guidelines, class rules, uncrewed-vessel rules and national law, and map the path from approval in principle to sea trials and a permit to operate. • Charging stations and data centres. Work out the approvals for quay-side chargers, ocean charging hubs and offshore data centres: siting, grid connection, safety and environmental clearances, and data rules. • Defence and government. Study defence procurement and export rules, government programmes, grants and maritime policy such as Sagarmala, and find where Waterfly fits. • Work with approvers. Prepare submissions and briefs for class societies such as Bureau Veritas and the Indian Register of Shipping, DG Shipping and maritime boards, and track every open requirement to closure. • Turn rules into requirements. Work with engineers to turn regulations into design requirements and test plans, from stability and propulsion drawings to cargo securing, so the evidence we produce matches what approvers need.What You’ll Bring • Structured research. You can read a 170-page regulation, find what applies to us, and summarise it in a page someone can act on. • Working technical knowledge, or the ability to build it fast: enough to discuss stability, batteries, charging and autonomy with engineers. • Clear writing. You can draft a submission, policy note or briefing that a regulator or founder can act on. • Confidence with senior stakeholders in government, defence and industry, and the patience to see a process through. • Attention to detail. You track requirements, deadlines and evidence without dropping a thread. • High ownership and speed. You care about getting the first cargo flying, not about whose job something is. • Good to have: exposure to maritime, aviation, energy or defence regulation; policy, legal or public-sector internships; familiarity with IMO, IEC or ISO standards; an interest in deep-tech hardware.

Job Description
About Waterfly Over water, shippers choose between ships that take days and aircraft that cost about 20 times more. Waterfly, incubated at IIT Madras, is building the mode in between: electric, autonomous craft that fly just above the sea at near-aircraft speed for a tenth of the cost of air freight. What to Expect We are hiring Management Consultants from the 2027 batch to map, and help shape, the rules that let a new kind of vehicle operate. You will work directly with the CEO and CBO, own a regulatory area within your first few months, and turn what you find into plans the company can act on. The role is full-time and based in Chennai, with travel to regulators, class societies and partners. You will join in summer 2027 and report to the CBO. Our craft fly a few metres above the water, so they are regulated as vessels, not aircraft: Type B wing-inground craft under IMO guidelines, and vessels under India’s Merchant Shipping Act, 2025. That is a faster path, but much of it has never been applied to an uncrewed, battery-electric craft with a blended wing-hull-body, or to the charging stations, offshore data centres, and defence and government uses around it. Your work decides how fast our 300 kg craft, flying autonomously since August 2026, and its successors reach paying customers. Expect direct mentorship from the founders, a seat in conversations with regulators and class societies early on, and enough engineering exposure to understand exactly what you are getting approved. What You’ll Do • Craft regulation. Study the rules for blended wing-hull-body craft and other new designs, including IMO wing-in-ground guidelines, class rules, uncrewed-vessel rules and national law, and map the path from approval in principle to sea trials and a permit to operate. • Charging stations and data centres. Work out the approvals for quay-side chargers, ocean charging hubs and offshore data centres: siting, grid connection, safety and environmental clearances, and data rules. • Defence and government. Study defence procurement and export rules, government programmes, grants and maritime policy such as Sagarmala, and find where Waterfly fits. • Work with approvers. Prepare submissions and briefs for class societies such as Bureau Veritas and the Indian Register of Shipping, DG Shipping and maritime boards, and track every open requirement to closure. • Turn rules into requirements. Work with engineers to turn regulations into design requirements and test plans, from stability and propulsion drawings to cargo securing, so the evidence we produce matches what approvers need.What You’ll Bring • Structured research. You can read a 170-page regulation, find what applies to us, and summarise it in a page someone can act on. • Working technical knowledge, or the ability to build it fast: enough to discuss stability, batteries, charging and autonomy with engineers. • Clear writing. You can draft a submission, policy note or briefing that a regulator or founder can act on. • Confidence with senior stakeholders in government, defence and industry, and the patience to see a process through. • Attention to detail. You track requirements, deadlines and evidence without dropping a thread. • High ownership and speed. You care about getting the first cargo flying, not about whose job something is. • Good to have: exposure to maritime, aviation, energy or defence regulation; policy, legal or public-sector internships; familiarity with IMO, IEC or ISO standards; an interest in deep-tech hardware.

About Waterfly Waterfly builds electric, autonomous craft that fly a few metres above the sea, moving cargo at nearaircraft speed for a tenth of the cost of air freight. We started at IIT Madras, build every craft in-house in Chennai, and aim to be the cheapest and fastest way to move goods across the world. What to Expect We are hiring Graduate Engineers from the 2027 batch to design, build and fly Pelican, our 10-tonne electric sea-skimming cargo craft. You will join a small team of generalist engineers who take the craft from a blank page to a flight test, and you will own a subsystem within your first few months. The role is full-time and based in Chennai, with travel to test sites. You will join in summer 2027 and report to the CTO. The engineering has no textbook answer yet. Flying in ground effect cuts drag and adds lift, giving better lift-to-drag in our tests, and that is what lets a battery-powered craft cover real distances. Our patent pending blended wing-hull-body has scaled from a 3 kg model in 2025 to the 300 kg Hummingbird, which has flown autonomously since August 2026. Aerodynamics, hydrodynamics, structures, batteries, avionics and autonomy sit in one team, so your calculations become carbon-fibre parts and flight data within weeks. Expect direct mentorship from the founders, fast and honest feedback, and a pace that picks up around test campaigns. Design. Size and design subsystems of an electric WIG craft: wings and hull, hydrofoils, composite structure, battery packs and motors, flight control and sensing. Start with hand calculations, then refine with CAD, CFD and FEA. • Build. Make what you design in our in-house workshop alongside our technicians: carbon-fibre layups and cures, wiring harnesses, battery assembly and avionics integration. • Test. Plan and run lake and sea trials. Instrument the craft, collect flight data, work out why something failed and fix it before the next run. • Battery cell research. Develop new battery cells from scratch: explore chemistries and electrode materials, build prototype cells, and test them for energy density, power, cycle life and safety, so our craft can fly further on every charge. • Composite research. Develop carbon-fibre layups, resin systems and cure processes, and test material coupons to make our structures lighter and stronger. • Document for certification. Produce the design, test and safety evidence that class societies such as Bureau Veritas and the Indian Register of Shipping need to approve a new type of vessel. • Work across the stack. Help teammates on other subsystems, take part in design reviews, and pick up whatever the craft needs that week. A strong grasp of physics and maths. You reach for a first-principles estimate before a simulation. • You have built real hardware, such as a competition vehicle, drone, rocket, robot, boat or your own project, and can explain what broke and why. • Depth in at least one area (aerodynamics or hydrodynamics, structures and composites, electrochemistry and battery cells, power electronics, or controls and embedded software) and real curiosity about the rest. • Comfort with the tools the work needs: CAD, FEA or CFD, Python or MATLAB, microcontrollers. Any subset is fine if you learn fast. • High ownership and speed. You care about getting the craft flying, not about whose job something is. • Clear writing. You can produce a test report that someone else can act on. • Good to have: hands-on composites fabrication or materials testing; battery cell fabrication or electrochemistry lab work; battery pack or motor-drive design; ArduPilot, PX4 or autonomy software; planing hulls, hydrofoils or free-surface CFD; or a student team such as Formula Student, solar car, aero-design, AUV or rocketry.

Job Description
About Waterfly Waterfly builds electric, autonomous craft that fly a few metres above the sea, moving cargo at nearaircraft speed for a tenth of the cost of air freight. We started at IIT Madras, build every craft in-house in Chennai, and aim to be the cheapest and fastest way to move goods across the world. What to Expect We are hiring Graduate Engineers from the 2027 batch to design, build and fly Pelican, our 10-tonne electric sea-skimming cargo craft. You will join a small team of generalist engineers who take the craft from a blank page to a flight test, and you will own a subsystem within your first few months. The role is full-time and based in Chennai, with travel to test sites. You will join in summer 2027 and report to the CTO. The engineering has no textbook answer yet. Flying in ground effect cuts drag and adds lift, giving better lift-to-drag in our tests, and that is what lets a battery-powered craft cover real distances. Our patent pending blended wing-hull-body has scaled from a 3 kg model in 2025 to the 300 kg Hummingbird, which has flown autonomously since August 2026. Aerodynamics, hydrodynamics, structures, batteries, avionics and autonomy sit in one team, so your calculations become carbon-fibre parts and flight data within weeks. Expect direct mentorship from the founders, fast and honest feedback, and a pace that picks up around test campaigns. Design. Size and design subsystems of an electric WIG craft: wings and hull, hydrofoils, composite structure, battery packs and motors, flight control and sensing. Start with hand calculations, then refine with CAD, CFD and FEA. • Build. Make what you design in our in-house workshop alongside our technicians: carbon-fibre layups and cures, wiring harnesses, battery assembly and avionics integration. • Test. Plan and run lake and sea trials. Instrument the craft, collect flight data, work out why something failed and fix it before the next run. • Battery cell research. Develop new battery cells from scratch: explore chemistries and electrode materials, build prototype cells, and test them for energy density, power, cycle life and safety, so our craft can fly further on every charge. • Composite research. Develop carbon-fibre layups, resin systems and cure processes, and test material coupons to make our structures lighter and stronger. • Document for certification. Produce the design, test and safety evidence that class societies such as Bureau Veritas and the Indian Register of Shipping need to approve a new type of vessel. • Work across the stack. Help teammates on other subsystems, take part in design reviews, and pick up whatever the craft needs that week. A strong grasp of physics and maths. You reach for a first-principles estimate before a simulation. • You have built real hardware, such as a competition vehicle, drone, rocket, robot, boat or your own project, and can explain what broke and why. • Depth in at least one area (aerodynamics or hydrodynamics, structures and composites, electrochemistry and battery cells, power electronics, or controls and embedded software) and real curiosity about the rest. • Comfort with the tools the work needs: CAD, FEA or CFD, Python or MATLAB, microcontrollers. Any subset is fine if you learn fast. • High ownership and speed. You care about getting the craft flying, not about whose job something is. • Clear writing. You can produce a test report that someone else can act on. • Good to have: hands-on composites fabrication or materials testing; battery cell fabrication or electrochemistry lab work; battery pack or motor-drive design; ArduPilot, PX4 or autonomy software; planing hulls, hydrofoils or free-surface CFD; or a student team such as Formula Student, solar car, aero-design, AUV or rocketry.

The role will entail working closely with the investment research team. You will be part of the entire investment process, beginning with idea generation, company evaluation, management meetings, channel checks and valuations. You will be working as part of sector teams covering designated sectors basis candidate preference/ firm requirements. As a part of the sector/ company specific research, you would be the part of the end-to-end investment process which would include, but not limited to: a) Idea generation: Identifying investable opportunities basis quantitative and qualitative factors b) Company Evaluation: Understanding the business model, growth drivers, competitive strengths, management capabilities and capital allocation, amongst others, to build an investment thesis c) Industry Analysis: Delineating market dynamics and structures, along with sectoral trends d) Stakeholder meetings: Participating actively in management, industry expert meetings/ conferences to generate actionable insights e) Due diligence and Channel Checks: Visiting relevant plants/ stores/ markets to improve on business understanding f) Financial Analysis: Analysing financial statements and building/ maintaining financial models, including proprietary models, for coverage companies g) Portfolio Tracking: Periodic tracking the business progress of coverage companies to monitor progress of investment thesis h) Research Discussions: Active participation in internal research discussions on ideas across the relevant investment universe Candidates are expected to pursue higher studies post the completion of the 2-year program. Exceptional performers in the program may be considered for a permanent role.

About the company	WhiteOak Capital group provides investment management and advisory services for equity assets of over USD 12 Bn as of June 2026, across the group. Besides segregated managed accounts for leading global institutions, WhiteOak offers investment services through a wide array of fund vehicles domiciled in India, Ireland, Mauritius, and UK to individual and institutional investors in India and worldwide. WhiteOak has investment research teams based in India, Singapore, and Spain, and additional sales and distribution offices across Asia and Europe. WhiteOak Capital group was founded by Mr. Prashant Khemka, former CIO of Goldman Sachs Asset Management’s India Equity and Global Emerging Markets Equity businesses. WhiteOak’s performance-first investment culture is founded upon the following four pillars; stock selection-based philosophy, high caliber research team, disciplined analytical process and balanced portfolio construction framework. Recently, White Oak has also launched 2 new initiatives – Global Emerging Markets (GEM) practice, covering over 40 emerging market economies, and a domestic Asset Management Company (AMC) business.

About the company	YCP India is a management consulting and advisory firm we founded in 2010 the objective of creating sustainable value for our clients. We have offices - Mumbai, Gurgaon, Delhi, Bangalore, Hyderabad. We work with our clients across diverse geographies including India, Southeast Asia, Europe, and Japan. Our projects involve working closely with our clients to address their most important strategic problems. There are two factors that drive our service offerings. The first is the diversity of our client base. It spans entrepreneurial growth businesses in their incubation phase, large diversified Indian conglomerates and western multi-nationals operating in India, government. The second is our desire to be long-term growth partners to our clients, not just project-specific consultants. Consequently, our service offerings span both strategy (aspiration setting, regulatory and policy analysis, growth strategy, resource allocation, risk management, bid advisory, valuation, and due diligence) and execution (planning & review, organization development, business incubation, project war rooms etc.) We believe we have been successful in this – we have clients who have partnered with us continuously over many years through multiple phases in their evolution. While our strategy development and execution processes are sector agnostic, till date, our work has largely been in technology, transportation (airports, highways, seaports), real estate, power (both conventional and renewable), construction, retail, consumer goods, healthcare and education, industrials, media and sports, big data and digital. Auctus Advisors Private Limited will now be known globally by its new name YCP India, as per the firm's integration into YCP Holdings (Global) Limited, which was first announced in November 2022. Since integrating, YCP India has extended its reach in India and beyond. Our respective histories, an expansive network of resources, and years of combined industry know-how help us maximize client's growth and potential for their success.

Infrastructure Developer Low-Latency Systems — HFT Technology About the role As an Infrastructure Developer on Zanskar Research's HFT Technology team, you will architect and engineer the ultra-low-latency trading stack that gives our strategies a measurable edge - measured in microseconds and nanoseconds. You will work at the intersection of systems programming, networking, and financial markets, solving some of the most technically demanding engineering problems in the industry. Key responsibilities — Design and develop low-latency order management systems (OMS) and execution infrastructure in C++ (17/20). — Build and optimise kernel-bypass networking components using DPDK, RDMA, or FPGA-based feed handlers for market data ingestion. — Implement and tune exchange connectivity (FIX, ITCH, OUCH, NSE/BSE native protocols) with nanosecond-precision timestamping. — Build and maintain automated testing pipelines including market simulation environments and replay-based regression testing. — Collaborate with quant researchers to deploy new strategies into production with safe, observable rollout processes. — Own reliability and observability: design alerting, circuit breakers, kill-switches, and real-time telemetry dashboards. — Continuously evaluate and integrate new hardware and software technologies to improve throughput and reduce jitter. Required qualifications — Currently pursuing a B.Tech / Dual Degree / M.Tech in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline - with a strong academic record. — Strong C++ proficiency (STL, templates, move semantics, memory model) with a clear understanding of performance implications of language constructs. — Deep knowledge of Linux internals: process/thread scheduling, memory subsystems, system calls, and kernel networking. — Solid understanding of CPU microarchitecture: cache hierarchy, branch prediction, instruction pipelining, SIMD. — Competence in data structures and algorithms - ability to reason about time and space complexity at a hardware level. Good to have — Hands-on exposure to HFT or real-time systems (internship, project, or personal work). — Familiarity with FPGA programming (VHDL/Verilog) or SmartNIC offload pipelines. — Knowledge of exchange market data protocols: ITCH, PITCH, FAST, or NSE/BSE proprietary feeds. — Proficiency in Python for tooling, test automation, and monitoring scripts. What we offer — Access to cutting-edge hardware: co-located servers, 10G/25G NICs, FPGA cards, and dedicated testing environments. — Work on problems where every microsecond genuinely matters - no artificial constraints or bureaucratic bottlenecks. — Rapid ownership: new hires own a production system component within their first 60 days. — Strong engineering culture with regular internal tech talks and hardware deep-dives.(Codeforces/AtCoder 1500+ rating or Codechef 1700+ rating) eligible

Job Description
Infrastructure Developer Low-Latency Systems — HFT Technology About the role As an Infrastructure Developer on Zanskar Research's HFT Technology team, you will architect and engineer the ultra-low-latency trading stack that gives our strategies a measurable edge - measured in microseconds and nanoseconds. You will work at the intersection of systems programming, networking, and financial markets, solving some of the most technically demanding engineering problems in the industry. Key responsibilities — Design and develop low-latency order management systems (OMS) and execution infrastructure in C++ (17/20). — Build and optimise kernel-bypass networking components using DPDK, RDMA, or FPGA-based feed handlers for market data ingestion. — Implement and tune exchange connectivity (FIX, ITCH, OUCH, NSE/BSE native protocols) with nanosecond-precision timestamping. — Build and maintain automated testing pipelines including market simulation environments and replay-based regression testing. — Collaborate with quant researchers to deploy new strategies into production with safe, observable rollout processes. — Own reliability and observability: design alerting, circuit breakers, kill-switches, and real-time telemetry dashboards. — Continuously evaluate and integrate new hardware and software technologies to improve throughput and reduce jitter. Required qualifications — Currently pursuing a B.Tech / Dual Degree / M.Tech in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline - with a strong academic record. — Strong C++ proficiency (STL, templates, move semantics, memory model) with a clear understanding of performance implications of language constructs. — Deep knowledge of Linux internals: process/thread scheduling, memory subsystems, system calls, and kernel networking. — Solid understanding of CPU microarchitecture: cache hierarchy, branch prediction, instruction pipelining, SIMD. — Competence in data structures and algorithms - ability to reason about time and space complexity at a hardware level. Good to have — Hands-on exposure to HFT or real-time systems (internship, project, or personal work). — Familiarity with FPGA programming (VHDL/Verilog) or SmartNIC offload pipelines. — Knowledge of exchange market data protocols: ITCH, PITCH, FAST, or NSE/BSE proprietary feeds. — Proficiency in Python for tooling, test automation, and monitoring scripts. What we offer — Access to cutting-edge hardware: co-located servers, 10G/25G NICs, FPGA cards, and dedicated testing environments. — Work on problems where every microsecond genuinely matters - no artificial constraints or bureaucratic bottlenecks. — Rapid ownership: new hires own a production system component within their first 60 days. — Strong engineering culture with regular internal tech talks and hardware deep-dives.(Codeforces/AtCoder 1500+ rating or Codechef 1700+ rating) eligible

About the company	Founded in 2018 and listed in 2026, Zetwerk is a global manufacturing platform that enables businesses to bring world-class products to life through a network of trusted suppliers and cutting-edge technology. As a managed marketplace for contract manufacturing, we connect global enterprises with small and medium manufacturers to deliver high-quality, cost-efficient, and timely solutions. Our operations span across India, the USA, Europe, Asia, and the Middle East, supported by multiple state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities and a strong network of over 10,000 supplier partners. Together, we serve thousands of customers across industries such as renewable energy, precision engineering, automotive, and electronics - helping them scale their manufacturing capabilities with reliability and precision.
